chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqub ibn Yazid and Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding
a man who struck a gazelle with his sword until he cut it into two halves — can he eat it? He said: 'Yes, he may eat from what follows the head, then leave the tail (rear half).'

key_terms.أَبَانَهُ: Cut it in two / severed it — from the root بان meaning to separate or sever completely
key_terms.الذَّنَبَ: The tail/rear — referring to the posterior half of the animal which is to be discarded
key_terms.مِمَّا يَلِي الرَّأْسَ: From what follows/is adjacent to the head — the front half of the animal

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating a gazelle cut in two by a sword during hunting according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules on a hunting scenario where a man's sword blow split a gazelle in two. The ruling permits eating the portion containing the head (the front half), while the tail portion (rear half) is to be left, following the principle that the head-side retains the lawfulness from the hunt. This reflects the Islamic jurisprudential principle that in cases of slaughter or hunting that produces two parts, the part connected to the head and site of the fatal blow is permissible.
word_analysis: he severed it (cut it in two)

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, and Yahya Bin Al Mubarak, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding
a man who struck a gazelle with his sword until he cut it into two. Can he eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, he can eat from what follows the head, then leave the tail’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid and Yahya ibn Mubarak from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “About the case of a man who strikes a deer with his sword until it is cut into two: if he can use it for food.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can use it for food, only the piece with the head and leave the tail.’”
